done_when: Forge's own pull requests no longer run the unused selection job, and the plugin check runs only when plugin files change

known.title: Plugin marketplace changes bypass the install check

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A pull request changes only the plugin marketplace manifest.
The filter omits `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, so that pull request starts no plugin workflow. [GitHub path filters](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/trigger-a-workflow#using-filters-to-target-specific-paths-for-pull-request-or-push-events). This is a shipped plugin distribution file: `tests/test_mod_native.py:24` validates it, and `tests/test_mod_install.py:74` uses it for the real Claude installation test. A bad marketplace source can therefore reach a release without those pull request checks. The ruling named the `src/forge/mod` subtree but did not account for this separately located manifest.
findings.title: Plugin marketplace changes bypass the install check

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - A workflow edit makes the plugin job depend on the selection job.
The named proof checks the selection guard and trigger text but never checks whether the plugin job can run. Adding `needs: selection` to that job would make it skip on every matching pull request while this test still passes. The exact `splitlines()` comparison also fails for equivalent YAML, such as changing quote style or reordering the two positive paths. The proof needs to check the effective plugin job outcome for matching and nonmatching paths.
findings.title: Gate: test_1_pull_requests_skip_selection_and_filter_plugin_changes

why: Forge's own CI runs a selection job on pull requests that nothing reads and runs the plugin check on every pull request, adding three jobs and queue waits to each push
